notes.meaning: Job paused to see whether his companions would offer any reply, but they remained silent. With no response coming from them, he took up his speech again to describe his former life and state his case before God.

Job yearned for the past months when he lived under God's watchful care. His deepest grief was not the loss of his wealth, but the painful feeling that God had stopped protecting and watching over him.
Job remembered how God's favor once guided him like an overhead lamp illuminating his path. With the Lord's clear guidance, he had moved safely through danger, calamity, and seasons of uncertainty.
He looked back at his mature years when his life was fruitful and secure. Most of all, he missed the close, friendly fellowship he shared with God within his own tent.
Job recalled the comfort of having the Almighty's gracious presence actively near him each day. In that season, his children were still alive and safely gathered all around his home.

Pictures of steps bathed in cream and oil pouring from stony ground describe vast pastoral wealth. Olive trees flourished even on rocky slopes, giving him an extraordinary abundance of rich provisions.
Job remembered walking to the city entrance to take his place in the public square. In ancient towns, the city gate was the community center where judges sat to settle disputes and govern fairly.
When Job walked into the assembly, young men stepped back out of awe and respect for his presence. Older community leaders, who were already seated, stood up to honor him.

City rulers and nobles stopped talking as soon as Job arrived, covering their mouths in respectful silence. Even influential leaders held their tongues because they valued his deep wisdom and fair decisions.

Those who heard Job's rulings called him blessed, and anyone who saw him in action praised his upright conduct. This public approval stood in direct contrast to the false charges his friends had leveled against him.
People honored Job because he used his authority to deliver the poor when they cried out for relief. He served as a protector to fatherless children who had no one else to stand up for them.
People on the brink of ruin blessed Job because he stepped in and saved them from destruction. He protected vulnerable widows from injustice, filling their hearts with gladness.

Job treated justice and fairness like garments he put on every single day. Doing what was right was not a temporary role for him, but an everyday habit that covered all his actions like a robe and turban.

Job helped those who could not help themselves by serving as eyes to the blind and feet to the lame. He provided guidance to people who lacked direction and supported those who were physically or socially helpless.

He cared for the poor with the compassion and protection of a loving father. When unfamiliar travelers or strangers had legal problems, he carefully investigated the facts to make sure they received fair treatment.
Job pictured evil oppressors as predatory beasts with dangerous fangs. He broke the power of violent men and snatched their innocent victims safely away from their grip.
In his days of blessing, Job assumed he would live to a peaceful old age and die quietly at home in his own bed. He expected his life to last for countless days, as numerous as grains of sand.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars and ancient translations read the Hebrew word for sand as the mythical phoenix, a bird said to die in its nest and live for centuries, matching the nest imagery in the first half of the line.

notes.meaning: Job compared his former life to a healthy tree whose roots reach deep into constant streams of water. With moisture from below and fresh dew resting on its branches every night, his life had remained green and strong.
His honor and good reputation stayed fresh without ever growing stale. Like a hunting bow that keeps its spring and power, his strength and ability to do good were constantly renewed.
When community matters were discussed, people waited quietly and listened with high expectations for Job's advice. They remained silent while he spoke because they trusted his wisdom.
Once Job gave his judgment, no one argued or felt the need to add anything more. His words settled gently on his listeners like refreshing dew, calming arguments and giving clear guidance.
People longed for his counsel just as farmers longed for rain on dry soil. They took in his words eagerly, like thirsty crops drinking in the spring showers that ripened the harvest.

When Job smiled at people who were discouraged, they could scarcely believe someone of such stature was so kind. His friendly, calm face lifted their spirits without ever reducing their deep respect for him.

Job directed the affairs of the people and led them with the authority of a king among his troops. Yet along with his high rank, he was gentle enough to sit beside hurting people and bring comfort to those who mourned.
